problem: R is defined as the stored volume "at the end of the active period", but the formula itself adds the compressed archive term (Vd × Dr) ÷ C, so R covers the active plus archive storage at the end of the archive period. As written, a student who reads the definition will compute only Vd × Da (900 GB in the example) instead of 1,175 GB, contradicting the worked example.
fix: Define R as the total stored volume at the end of the archive period, in GB (active copies plus compressed archive copies). In the example, R = 1,175 GB at day 364, while storage at the end of the active period alone is Vd × Da = 900 GB.

problem: "Data protection is the set of controls" narrows data protection to technical controls. In law and in standard usage, data protection is the legal and regulatory duty to safeguard personal data and the rights of the person it belongs to (consent, purpose limitation, erasure), which is wider than security controls.
fix: Say that data protection is the legal and policy duty to safeguard personal data and honour the data subject's rights, and data security is the set of technical and organisational controls that carry it out. Data retention is one rule inside that duty.

where: Worked example 1, step 5, and the figure purge bar
problem: The example says the service writes 10 GB of logs per day, then reports 0 GB after the purge window. If writes continue, day 365 to day 395 adds 30 more days of logs (300 GB) and the last 90 days of logs are still inside their active retention at day 365, so they cannot be purged. The zero figure only holds if the tracked data set stops at day 365.
fix: State the assumption: the purge applies to the log set written up to day 365 and no new logs are counted. Otherwise the answer is 300 GB of new active logs after the purge, and the data older than the 90-day active window is what gets purged.
